title: EconSprint Velocity — Adaptive Budgets & Guardrail Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Pilot an operational playbook that pairs adaptive budget bands (per-route token budgets and cost gates) with lightweight runtime guardrails (elastic batch shims, KV-ttl governance, and model-specific quant profiles). Goal: deliver measurable per-token cost reduction while preserving user-facing quality and latency SLOs.
objectives: Reduce median per-token cost for targeted routes by >= 15% within the pilot cohort
Keep 99th percentile latency within existing SLOs for high-priority routes
Maintain >95% pass rate on our quality regression suite for trial prompts
KPIs: Per-token cost delta (baseline vs pilot) — target -15%
Latency P95 and P99 for pilot routes — no more than 5% regression
Quality regression pass rate on seeded prompts — >=95%
Rolling weekly savings captured and projected annualized savings
experiment_grid: Elastic Batch Shims (EBS): dynamic batch targets that shrink at high tail latency; variants A/B/C
KV-ttl governance: per-model prefix TTL and hot-prefix size cap — test small/medium/large
Model Quant Profiles: int8 fast-path vs mixed-precision baseline with quality gating
Budget Bands: route-level soft budget with automated fallback to cheaper model variant
Combined bundle: EBS + KV-ttl + quant-profile vs control
updates: 2026-02-18 — Kickoff: scoped 12 pilot routes across 3 customers. Shared kickoff doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcEconSprintKickoff
2026-02-25 — Eng spike completed: prototype EBS runtime hook merged to feature branch. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821 (ENG review pending)
2026-03-03 — Design review: UX for 'budget exceeded' telemetry and console alert patterns. Design notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/UX-Budget-Alerts
2026-03-08 — PM / Eng sync: narrowed pilot to routes with predictable seq-length distributions to reduce noise. Action: add seq-length filter to experiment harness (ENG-3890)
2026-03-12 — First field deployment (canary): EBS variant A deployed to 10% of traffic on two internal routes. Early telemetry shows 6% cost delta and +1.8% P95 latency — within guardrail thresholds.
decisions: Adopt soft budgets (non-blocking) for initial rollout to avoid broken customer flows
Require model-specific quant-profile canary with runbook rollback on quality tests failing below 95%
Use 'elastic batch shim' as the primary latency-aware batching mechanism rather than static batch caps
next_steps: Expand canary to 25% for selected low-latency routes on 2026-03-20 pending ops signoff
Run quant-profile canary on 1 customer sandbox and validate quality suite by 2026-03-22
Implement automated budget gating in control plane: alpha API for soft enforcement (PM spec due 2026-03-18)
Define final rollout decision criteria and handover checklist for Dedicated customers
risks: Quality regressions for long-tail prompt families if quant profiles are too aggressive
Unanticipated latency spikes when EBS interacts with autoscaling bursts
Telemetry noise making signal detection slow — need stricter histogram bucketing and seq-length bucketing
notes: Keep pilot routes isolated by customer to simplify billing signal attribution
Include a manual rollback button in console during canaries to expedite mitigation
Plan a cross-functional retro after pilot ends to transition playbook into 'EconOps Runbook'
